_: Where this fork hooks into upstream-owned files. fork/sync.mjs checks these after every replay: a merge can be textually clean and still lose a hook (upstream moved or rewrote the code around it). `min` is how many times the literal text must appear. When a port moves a hook, update the entry.

electron/main.ts.why: the gate holds every backend start and dial: runHermesStart, runPoolBackendStart and connectRegistryBackend (SSH / remote connections)
every outbound request of Electron's network stack is held until the tunnel is up
sessions created later (link titles, webviews) get the egress gate too
the update check (git / Python / feed fetches the egress gate can not see) waits for the tunnel; it lives in checkUpdates()
the tunnel is brought up as early as possible
the monitor is stopped on quit
at startup, an old fork bundle on a newer official runtime hands over to fork/update.mjs and boots nothing (electron/fork-update.ts)
a failed or postponed fork update is told to the user once
a build outside a fork checkout (an installer given to someone) has no 'Update now': the official update would leave it stale; it answers 'external'
the self-update shell is wired to the real app, git, the update marker and the VPN
the VPN IPC surface the renderer talks to
own AppUserModelID: own taskbar button and icon next to the official Hermes

electron/preload.ts.why: the renderer bridge for the VPN IPC surface

src/app/gateway/hooks/use-gateway-boot.t.why: the renderer's boot waits for main's gate instead of racing it
the renderer's boot budget renews while a first-run install is in progress, so a healthy install is not shown as "Hermes couldn't start" after 3 minutes (src/lib/with-timeout.ts)

src/app/contrib/wiring.tsx.why: the boot card that explains what the gate is waiting for
